scenes.title: Where and when
narration: Inai dance originates from the Malay court tradition and is performed during the circumcision ceremonies of palace children.
It is popular in Perlis, northern Kedah, and Kelantan.
Historically, it was performed by two men and is linked to significant palace events such as weddings, coronations, and circumcisions.

scenes.title: When it is danced
narration: Inai is performed during palace children's circumcision ceremonies, weddings, and royal coronations.
The Perak variant is linked to henna leaf picking nights (Berinai Kecil and Berinai Besar).
It marks important rites of passage and royal celebrations.
Today it is a living tradition.

scenes.title: Listen
narration: Inai dance is accompanied by Gendang Terinai, playing three songs: Temang Welo, Selong, and Mak Inang.
The Perak variant uses drums, gongs, and flutes.
Listen for the drums, gongs, flutes, gendang (drum).
The music features traditional Malay percussion instruments with rhythmic drum beats and melodic gong and flute lines, creating a formal and ceremonial atmosphere.

scenes.title: The people
narration: The main variant is the court dance in Perlis, northern Kedah, and Kelantan, performed by men.
Inai is a Malay court dance with influences from Mak Yong and Silat, reflecting a blend of dance-drama, martial arts, and acrobatic elements within Malay royal culture.
